title: Safety and tolerability of temporal interference stimulation in humans: A systematic review and meta-analysis of an emerging deep neuromodulation technology
title_zh: 人类中时域干扰刺激的安全性与耐受性：一种新兴深层神经调制技术的系统综述与荟萃分析
abstract: BACKGROUND: Temporal interference stimulation (TIS) uses kilohertz-frequency currents to generate a low-frequency amplitude-modulated envelope within brain tissue, enabling deeper targeting while minimizing superficial stimulation. As human applications expand, a systematic evaluation of safety and tolerability is needed. METHODS: Following PRISMA guidelines (PROSPERO: CRD420251081135), we searched Ovid MEDLINE, Embase, and APA PsycINFO (May 2, 2025) for peer-reviewed human TIS studies reporting safety or tolerability outcomes. Methodological quality and risk of bias were assessed using design-appropriate RoB 2, ROBINS-I, and Joanna Briggs Institute tools. Random-effects meta-analyses were conducted in R. Parallel-arm randomized controlled trials (RCTs) were synthesized using risk ratios (RRs), with sensitivity analyses using risk differences (RDs), alternative continuity corrections, and pooling models. Within-subject studies were summarized descriptively using pooled adverse event (AE) proportions, with additional sensitivity analyses by transformation, study quality, and AE-elicitation method. RESULTS: Twenty-four studies (N = 853 participants; 21 RCTs, 3 non-randomized) were included. No serious AEs (SAEs) were reported. In parallel-arm RCTs (k = 5 arms; N = 192 participants), most AEs showed effects near null. Tingling was more frequent with active TIS (RR = 2.95; 95% CI, 1.25-7.00; RD = 0.18; 95% CI, 0.01-0.34). In within-subject studies (k = 20 arms; N = 531 participants), descriptive pooled AE proportions varied across outcomes, with the highest estimates observed for fatigue, sleepiness, and tingling. DISCUSSION: TIS was generally well tolerated in humans, with predominantly mild, transient AEs and no SAEs reported. Evidence is limited to conservative parameters (~2 kHz; ≤2 mA/channel), small sample sizes, and short-term TIS applications.
abstract_zh: 背景：时域干扰刺激（TIS）利用千赫兹频率电流在脑组织内产生低频幅度调制包络，从而实现更深层靶向，同时减少表层刺激。随着人类应用的扩展，需要对其安全性和耐受性进行系统评估。方法：依据PRISMA指南（PROSPERO: CRD420251081135），我们在2025年5月2日对Ovid MEDLINE、Embase和APA PsycINFO进行了检索，筛选报告人类TIS安全或耐受性结果的同行评议研究。使用与研究设计相适应的RoB 2、ROBINS‑I和Joanna Briggs Institute工具评估方法学质量与偏倚风险。采用R软件进行随机效应荟萃分析。并行组随机对照试验（RCT）使用风险比（RR）进行合成，并通过风险差（RD）、不同连续性校正和汇聚模型进行敏感性分析。受试者内研究采用描述性汇总，计算合并不良事件（AE）比例，并通过变换、研究质量和AE诱发方法进行额外敏感性分析。结果：共纳入24项研究（共853名参与者；21项RCT，3项非随机化研究）。未报告严重不良事件（SAE）。在并行组RCT中（k=5组；N=192），大多数AE的效应接近零。刺痛在活跃TIS组更为频繁（RR=2.95；95% CI, 1.25-7.00；RD=0.18；95% CI, 0.01-0.34）。在受试者内研究中（k=20组；N=531），描述性合并AE比例在不同结果间差异显著，疲劳、嗜睡和刺痛的估计比例最高。讨论：TIS在人体中总体耐受性良好，主要表现为轻度、短暂的不良事件，未报告SAE。现有证据受限于保守参数（约2 kHz；≤2 mA/通道）、样本量小以及短期TIS应用。
